body:
Problem:  An autocommand that redraws may do so while curwin is
          temporarily set for the autocommand scope. This can result in
          flickering or unexpected state with UI components (statusline,
          winbar, decor providers...) that depend on the current window.
          Current workaround for statusline and winbar specifically
          delays the redraw, which can itself be unexpected for the
          autocommand.
Solution: If redrawing happens with a temporary autocmd current window,
          temporarily restore the current window while redrawing.

fix https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/40153

comment_regular_data.body:
I kept your tests mostly intact @barrettruth, removing the mentions of delayed redrawing.
@bfredl @zeertzjq do you see foresee any problems with this approach? Ref #40309
i was looking at this currently. too late. i'll leave another comment in a bit.

this introduces a change in behavior - maybe a regression maybe not depending on how you view it. specifically, window-local variables are not kept.

```vim
set hidden
call setline(1, 'bb')
autocmd User <buffer> let w:x = 7 | redraw! | let g:after = get(w:, 'x', -1)
enew
doautoall User
echo g:after
```

Before: 7
After: -1

In the above example, we can see the makes `:redraw` clear window-local variables from the active autocmd window in the middle of an autocmd for a hidden buffer. this is sort of a weird case but it definitely seems like too much side effect for a redraw.

@luukvbaal 

I do get the "let's try it" mindset but I'd like to at least review next time :sweat_smile:

does this handle nesting or do we care?

AI had this callout:

> The two call sites guard re-entry differently:
>
> - `update_screen`: restore when `curwin != save`, re-enter when `curwin != new` → balanced inverse pair.
> - `win_redr_custom`: restore when `curwin != save`, re-enter when `curwin == new.
>
> Trace win_redr_custom called standalone while in a temp context (curwin == new, new != save):
> 1. top: curwin != save → aucmd_restbuf → now curwin == save
> 2. theend: curwin == new? No (curwin == save, and save != new) → no re-enter
> 3. returns with curwin left at the real window — the temp aucmd context is silently dropped.
>
> `win_redr_custom` is reachable standalone (e.g. `win_redr_ruler` at statusline.c:499, `draw_tabline`)

This is not right in totality, i favor a revert.

the window context is not symmetrically restored in win_redr_custom, such as with `nvim__redraw({ buf = ev.buf, statusline = true, flush = false })`.

idk about the ai analysis.

NGL, this code (all of the inherited autocmd code, not this pr XD) is way too complicated and is wasting too much time. I feel like the only next thing to do here is to refactor all of it in favor of simplicity before more tweaks like this.

> NGL, this code (all of the inherited autocmd code, not this pr XD) is way too complicated and is wasting too much time. I feel like the only next thing to do here is to refactor all of it in favor of simplicity before more tweaks like this.

Definitely true, but the good news is that hardening `aucmd_prepbuf` is very worthwhile, because it is an abstraction that the system can use, and all the nasty stuff lives in that abstraction. That abstraction gives us hope for potential simplifications or a redesign later.

The problem is when distant parts (such as `update_screen`, etc) have to coordinate, and yes that's usually a bad sign, bc it's not really an "abstraction" due to fragility.
Can we still revert this? I'd like to discuss more with luukvbaal. It tangibly introduces the aforementioned failure. Not to say the approach doesn't have merit, I would like to refine it more.

we can, but i'm not in a rush to do so. unless there's a failing test or concrete bug? maybe an adjustment can be made? this approach is definitely more attractive that the redraw special case, though neither is ideal...
In the above example, this patch wipes window-local variables for autocmds run on hidden buffer. That is a bug

Yes this PR was made under the assumption that aucmd_prep/restbuf would have no side-effects. I should have taken a closer look, sorry. I guess what may suffice here is just manually restoring the current window temporarily, avoiding the restbuf cleanup.

lmk if you want to work on this or not; just assign me as reviewer if so

all good
